carousel_c1.label: Discernment
carousel_c1.title: 5 questions to ask before you decide God told you something

carousel_c1.a: If yes, stop. That settles it, and nothing else on this list matters.

carousel_c1.q: Would I want this to be God’s voice?
carousel_c1.a: Wanting it doesn’t make it false. It does mean you need more than your own certainty.
People who know you and will tell you the truth. Not people who’ll agree.
If the honest answer is nothing, wait.

carousel_c1.q: Am I asking for direction, or for permission?
carousel_c1.a: You already know which one this is.

carousel_c2.label: Prayer journalling
carousel_c2.title: How to keep a prayer journal you’ll actually re-read

carousel_c2.q: One thread per thing you’re carrying.
carousel_c2.a: Not one notebook for everything. Several threads running at once — because life isn’t one subject at a time.

carousel_c2.q: Anchor every entry to a passage.
carousel_c2.a: Feelings without scripture attached won’t mean much to you in six months.

carousel_c2.q: Write the question, not the conclusion.

carousel_c2.a: The pattern only shows up when you can see the order it arrived in.
This is the step everyone skips. It is also the only one that matters.

carousel_c2.kicker: The writing is easy. The re-reading is the work.
carousel_c2.title: Ponder does all five by default.

carousel_c3.label: Scripture
carousel_c3.title: 6 passages for when you can’t tell if it’s God or you

carousel_c3.text: “…and after the fire a still small voice.”
carousel_c3.note: Not in the wind. Not in the earthquake.
Including your understanding of what you’re hearing.

carousel_c3.text: “Search me, God, and know my heart.”
“If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God.”
“The heart is deceitful above all things.”
carousel_c3.note: Read this one alongside the others — never instead of them.

carousel_c4.label: How Ponder works
carousel_c4.title: Why a devotional should ask hard questions

carousel_c4.a: It is most of what this category offers, and there is nothing wrong with it. Some days it is exactly what you need.

carousel_c4.q: But if every entry confirms you,
carousel_c4.a: you are not discerning. You are rehearsing something you already decided.

carousel_c4.q: So one entry in four is a challenge entry.
carousel_c4.a: Clearly labelled, so you know the posture before you read a word of it.
Or offers a counterpoint from scripture. Or asks something harder than you would ask yourself.
Hard questions, asked gently. And you control how often they appear.

carousel_c0.title: A daily devotional for the thread you’re actually carrying.

carousel_c0.q: Name it in your own words.
carousel_c0.a: “Trusting God with my business.” “Learning to be still.” Whatever it is you keep coming back to.

carousel_c0.q: Scripture comes to it. Every day.
carousel_c0.a: A passage, a short reflection, an illustration to sit with, questions, and directions for prayer.
Every note collects into one journal for that thread — so months of scattered thoughts read as a single arc.
God rarely works on one thing at a time. Neither does life.
